caption: Figure 1: Architecture and training procedure. Stages 1–3 describe the three-stage training scheme. A variance-correction network returns $\Delta V _ { \phi } ( \mathbf { x } )$ , multiplied by a deterministic maturity function $g ( \tau )$ so that the correction vanishes as $\tau 0$ . Prices are produced by substituting the resulting efective variance into the Black–Scholes call formula, yielding $u _ { \phi } ( \mathbf { x } )$ (not the standard BS price unless $\Delta V _ { \phi } \equiv 0 )$ . A separate network outputs the compensated jump contribution $J _ { \psi } ( \mathbf { x } )$ . Greeks are obtained by automatic diferentiation of $u _ { \phi }$ The jump-PIDE residual $R ( \mathbf { x } )$ is computed and penalized at randomly sampled points. Stages 1–3 depict the three-stage training scheme used for jump-term identifiability.
Figure 2: Three-stage model: true vs predicted (price, delta, gamma, vega) on validation. (a) Price residuals ub <sup>−</sup> u.
(b) PIDE residual R(x) (three-stage). Figure 3: Error distributions for the three-stage model.
